title: Houston Dash fire coach Fabrice Gautrat and technical director Twila Kilgore with immediate effect
content:
The Houston Dash announced multiple changes to their coaching ranks Sunday, with two-year head coach Fabrice Gautrat stepping down and technical director Twila Kilgore leaving the club. Jaime Frias, who was hired as an assistant coach last year, will serve as interim head coach for the remainder of the season.

The club said that Gautrat and Kilgore, a former interim head coach with the U.S. women’s national team, “will transition away from their current roles.” A club spokesperson confirmed the pair will depart from the club immediately.

Club leadership is searching for the team’s next head coach.

“Our conviction in this group has not wavered,” Angela Hucles Mangano, the club’s president of women’s soccer, said in a statement. “We believe in the quality of this team and its ability to succeed both this season and beyond. We also have a responsibility to evaluate our trajectory and determine what is needed to achieve the ambitions we have for this team. Ultimately, this decision reflects our commitment to those ambitions and our determination to continue moving the club forward.”

With six games remaining in the regular season, the Dash sit 12th with a 7-12-5 (win-loss-draw) record in the 16-team NWSL. The team’s last win was a 5-0 victory over the last-placed Chicago Stars on Aug. 19.

Gautrat joined the club as its sixth head coach ahead of the 2025 season, finishing the year with an 8-12-6 record and 6 points shy of the postseason. Kilgore first joined the club as an assistant coach from 2019 to 2021, while simultaneously rising in the coaching ranks of the U.S. national team circuit. In 2023, she was named interim head coach of the senior women’s team, before Emma Hayes’ arrival.

“We want to thank Fabrice and Twila for their commitment to the organization and the work they have done on behalf of this organization,” Hucles Mangano said. “They have invested significantly in our players and our club, and we are grateful for their contributions. We wish them both continued success in their careers.”

Gautrat’s and Kilgore’s departures come as various NWSL clubs are reshuffling their coaching departments. The Kansas City Current recently parted ways with former head coach Vlatko Andonovski, who moved into a sporting director role after a historic 2025 season with the club. In Orlando, the Pride recently parted ways with Seb Hines, who guided the club to its first NWSL championship in 2024. On the West Coast, Bay FC is close to appointing ex-Chelsea general manager Paul Green as its head of football.

At the national team level, U.S. Soccer is also restructuring its sporting department and is on track to hire two new leaders: a director of women’s and girls’ soccer and a director of men’s and boys’ soccer, as The Athletic previously reported.
